_readme: THE GETTING-STARTED GUIDE, WRITTEN ONCE.
Two surfaces render this file and nothing else may: the in-app help topic
(HelpTopicID.gettingStarted, through the generated Swift twin
ios/WingFoilKit/Sources/WingFoilKit/Help/GettingStartedGuide.swift) and the web page
web/start/index.html, between its <!-- guide:begin --> and <!-- guide:end --> markers.
Both are written by web/tools/make_start.py; --check fails when either is stale.
The app shows a route's title and summary. The web shows title, summary and steps.
Budgets, the same ones HelpBudgetTests enforces: a summary, a step detail, a
troubleshooting detail and a report detail are 30 words each; the framing is 45.
THE ORDER OF `routes` IS THE ORDER BOTH SURFACES PRINT, and it follows the site's one
rule for watches: Apple Watch comes right after Garmin. Garmin, the CleanJibe Apple
Watch app, Apple's Workout app, any .fit, Strava. The release hides the two Apple
routes, so an App Store build reads Garmin, .fit, Strava and the order still holds.
`class` is a route's recording class, as an id of docs/copy/recording-classes.json:
a, bPlus, b, c. make_start.py reads that file for the name, so the pill on the web card
and the `classID` of the Swift twin say what the kit says. The two extras are notes
rather than routes and carry none.
`channels` lists the channels that HAVE the door a route describes (docs/channels.md).
The two Apple routes are beta-only, so the App Store build never names them: it reaches
them through the help topic's `related` topics instead.
`surfaces` says where an entry is rendered. Everything is on both unless it says
otherwise: the troubleshooting list and the report checklist are web-only (the app has
its own troubleshooting topics), and the line naming the web page is app-only.
`notice` is a route's one warning, web only: the card shows it above the fold, beside
the class pill, so a reader sees it before choosing the route. The Strava card carries
the seat cap there (rider review S5, 9 Oct 2026). The app says the same thing on the
screen that connects, so its help topic shows no notice.
`browser` is a route's line for the browser app, web only: the card prints it above the
fold, under the summary, so every way in says what the third app does with it (rider review
S10, 9 Oct 2026). A route the browser cannot take says so and names the way round. The
app's help topic is the iPhone's own and shows no browser line.
`webPage` says which page of the site an extra is printed on: "start" (the default) or
"beta". /start/ installs and gets the first session in; /beta/ says what to test and what
a good report says (rider review S9, 9 Oct 2026). The report checklist is on /beta/ too.
The app's help topic lists every extra whatever its page.
`{site}` becomes Branding.site in Swift and cleanjibe.org on the web.
`**bold**` is markdown in the app and <strong> on the web; *italic* likewise.
framing: Ride one session as you always do, then open it in CleanJibe. Every turn gets a verdict: flew through, touchdown, or fell in. We ride too, so tell us where it read one of yours wrong.

app.topicSummary: Your first session on the water, and where to send what you find.
paragraphs: Ride with the watch you already have. Your session comes into CleanJibe, and every turn gets a verdict.

On a Garmin, ride as always, with Windsurf or any other watersport profile. Set up intervals.icu once in Settings → intervals.icu. It is free, takes about 5 minutes, and your old sessions come in too.
Want more out there? The CleanJibe watch app buzzes each verdict on your wrist. It counts your pump strokes and takeoff attempts, and keeps your dry streak on the glass.
You can also open a .fit file straight from Files, Mail or a message. It can be yours, or one a friend sent you.
We ride too. We built CleanJibe for the jibes we were chasing ourselves.

routes.title: The ways in, one per watch
routes.lede: Take the way in that matches your wrist. Go outside, because every one of them needs GPS and a watch indoors records no positions. They all end the same way. Your session lands in CleanJibe, analysed as it arrives.
routes.betaLegend: in the public beta today, not yet in the App Store release.

troubleshooting.title: If something does not work
troubleshooting.lede: Try the line that matches. Then tell us how it went, either way.

test.title: What to test
test.lede: Five steps, after one ordinary session. The first one matters most.

report.title: What a good report says
report.lede: Keep it short. A screenshot of the session page beats a paragraph. "This number looks wrong" is a good report.

routes.title: Garmin, as you ride today
routes.status: fenix, epix, Forerunner and the rest
routes.summary: Ride as always, with Windsurf or any watersport profile. Connect intervals.icu once, and your old sessions come in too. The CleanJibe watch app adds verdicts on your wrist.
routes.browser: Paste your intervals.icu key into its Settings. Your Garmin sessions arrive there too, on any computer or phone.

steps.title: Ride as always
steps.detail: Record with Garmin's Windsurf profile, or SUP, Kitesurf or Surfing. CleanJibe takes every watersport session, and anything named wing or foil.

steps.title: Connect intervals.icu once
steps.detail: Make a free account at intervals.icu and connect Garmin there. Copy your personal API key into Settings → **intervals.icu**. It takes about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Your old sessions come in too
steps.detail: CleanJibe brings in your last two years of sessions and analyses each one as it lands. After a ride, pull down on Sessions and the new one is on top.

steps.title: Want more? Install the watch app
steps.detail: **CleanJibe Wingfoil Tracker (Beta)** on Connect IQ buzzes each verdict on your wrist. It counts pump strokes and takeoff attempts, and shows your dry streak.

steps.title: Record and save with it
steps.detail: Press START, pick **CleanJibe**, wait for GPS good and press START again. To finish, press START to pause, then BACK and **Save**.

steps.title: No intervals.icu? The long way
steps.detail: Garmin Connect's phone app cannot export. On a computer, connect.garmin.com → the activity → gear icon → **Export File**. AirDrop it to the iPhone, then Import → **FIT or ZIP…**.

steps.title: Garmin calls it Windsurf
steps.detail: Garmin has no wingfoil profile, so Garmin and Strava call the session Windsurf. With the watch app, Garmin Connect also shows foil time and flights. Strava does not.

routes.title: The CleanJibe Apple Watch app
routes.status: Apple Watch · everything a Garmin gets
routes.summary: Install it with the CleanJibe beta and record on your wrist. The watch only records, and the iPhone does the analysis.
routes.browser: This way in needs the iPhone app. A browser cannot reach your watch.

steps.title: Put it on the watch
steps.detail: It comes with the CleanJibe beta. On the iPhone open Apple's **Watch** app, scroll to *Available apps*, and install **CleanJibe** if it is missing.

steps.title: Record
steps.detail: Open CleanJibe on the watch, allow Health and Location if it asks, wait until NO GPS clears, press START. Then Stop, and Done.

steps.title: Let it arrive
steps.detail: Open CleanJibe on the iPhone. The session comes across on its own while phone and watch are together. Give it a minute.

steps.title: What you get
steps.detail: Speed comes off the watch's own receiver, so the records are measured. The 50 Hz wrist gives pump strokes and takeoff attempts.

routes.title: Apple's own Workout app
routes.summary: No extra app on the watch: record a Surfing workout and import it from Apple Health.
routes.browser: This way in needs the iPhone app. Apple Health is closed to a browser.

steps.title: Start a Surfing workout
steps.detail: On the watch open **Workout** and pick **Surfing**. *Water Sports* works too. Apple Health has no wingfoil activity, so pick the closest one.

steps.title: Ride, then end the workout
steps.detail: End it on the watch and let it save. The route is written to Health when the workout finishes, which can take a minute.

steps.title: Import it on the iPhone
steps.detail: Import → **Apple Health**. Allow CleanJibe to read workouts and routes. Switch every one on, or there is nothing to read. Then pick yours.

steps.title: Keep it automatic
steps.detail: Switch on *Import new Health workouts automatically* and the next session is waiting when you open the app.

steps.title: What you get
steps.detail: Speed comes off the watch's own receiver, so the records are measured. Nothing records your wrist, so there are no pump strokes or takeoff attempts.

routes.title: Any watch that writes a .fit
routes.status: Polar, Suunto, COROS and everything else
routes.summary: Sync it through intervals.icu, or share the file into CleanJibe from Files, Mail, AirDrop or any share sheet.
routes.browser: Drop the .fit into it, on a computer or any phone. The file never leaves the tab.

steps.title: Record on your own watch
steps.detail: Any outdoor activity with GPS, recorded the way you always do. There is nothing of ours to install on these watches.

steps.title: Export the workout as a file
steps.detail: Suunto: Calendar → the workout → ⋯ → FIT. COROS: Activities → the activity → ⋯ → Export → FIT. Polar exports from flow.polar.com only.

steps.title: Take the FIT where you are offered one
steps.detail: A FIT carries the speed your watch measured. A .gpx does not. A .tcx carries it only when the app wrote it in.

steps.title: Hand it to CleanJibe
steps.detail: **Open in CleanJibe** from the iOS share sheet, or Import → **FIT or ZIP…**. Foil time, flights, turns and the map are identical either way.

steps.title: Or let intervals.icu do it
steps.detail: Most of these watches sync to intervals.icu too. CleanJibe picks them up from there, through the same 4 steps as the Garmin route.

routes.title: Strava
routes.status: any watch that syncs to Strava
routes.notice: Strava lets a new app connect a limited number of riders. If connecting is refused, export the original on strava.com from a computer and import that file.
routes.summary: Settings → Strava → Connect with Strava, then Import → Import from Strava…. Strava keeps your track but not your watch's speed, so records are estimated.
routes.browser: Strava sign-in needs the iPhone app. Export Original on strava.com gives you a file the browser app opens.

steps.title: Connect once
steps.detail: Settings → **Strava** → Connect with Strava. Strava's own consent page opens. Leave the private-activities box ticked, or your "Only you" sessions stay hidden.

steps.title: Pick your sessions
steps.detail: Import → **Import from Strava…** lists your matching activities of the last two years. Tap the ones you want, or **Import all new**.

steps.title: Keep it automatic
steps.detail: Once one session has come in this way a toggle appears, and CleanJibe checks Strava whenever you open the app.

steps.title: What it costs
steps.detail: Strava hands over positions rather than the speed your watch measured. These speed records are marked **estimated**. There are no pump strokes.

steps.title: If connecting is refused
steps.detail: Strava lets a new app connect a limited number of riders. That is nothing to do with your account. Tell us through Menu → Support & ideas.

steps.title: Strava full? Take the file
steps.detail: On a computer, open the activity on strava.com and choose ⋯ → **Export Original**. AirDrop it to the iPhone, then Import → **FIT or ZIP…**.

extras.title: No wind today?
extras.summary: Record a 3 to 5 minute walk on the watch. It arrives in CleanJibe like a session would, so you know the whole way in works.

steps.title: 3 to 5 minutes of movement
steps.detail: A bike ride draws the nicest track. Anything above about 12 km/h counts as flying. Walking works too. Go outside: indoors there are no positions.

steps.title: Bring it in your own way
steps.detail: Take whichever way in above matches your watch. It answers one question: does a recording made on your watch reach CleanJibe on your phone?

steps.title: What you should see
steps.detail: A map shows your track, with duration and speeds at the top. A speed chart moves when you drag along it.

steps.title: Turns and jibes reading zero
steps.detail: Expected on a bike or on foot: there is nothing to jibe. This checks the way in from the watch, never the analysis.

extras.title: Tell us what you saw
extras.summary: Menu → Support & ideas opens a mail to us, with your app and watch details already in it. Your mail decides what we build next.

steps.title: Read the verdicts against your memory
steps.detail: Open the session and go to **Turns**. Every turn says *flew through*, *touchdown* or *fell in*. The clean jibes are marked among them.

steps.title: Say where it disagrees with you
steps.detail: Maybe it marked a jibe you flew through as a touchdown. Maybe it missed a time you fell in, or found a wind you did not sail in.

steps.title: Send it from the app
steps.detail: Menu → **Support & ideas** fills in your build, phone, iOS version, watch and library size. You add what happened and press Send.

steps.title: Attach the file if a session read wrong
steps.detail: With the .fit we can run the detection again and fix it. Without it there is only guesswork. Ideas and wishes are as welcome as faults.

steps.title: Send a card, and say how it reads
steps.detail: The share button on the session page draws a **share card** with your track and your numbers. Send it to a friend. Say if anything on it reads wrong.

settings._note: One sentence each, at the top of the matching Settings section. The app reads them from GettingStartedGuide, so the help and the switches say the same thing.
settings.intervalsIcu: Your Garmin sessions arrive here by themselves, your old ones too. Garmin has no open API, so intervals.icu is the bridge. Connect your Garmin there once. It is free.
settings.strava: Any watch that syncs to Strava works, with no file to move. Strava keeps your track but not your watch's speed, so the records are estimated.

entries.term: The watch app does not start
entries.detail: Restart the watch once. If it still does not start, send us the message it shows.
The workout is not in Health yet, or CleanJibe may not read it. Check iPhone Settings → Health → Data Access & Devices → CleanJibe, everything on.

entries.term: The watch says NO GPS for more than a minute
entries.detail: Open sky, wrist still, wait. A balcony under a roof is not open sky.

entries.term: The session never reaches the iPhone
entries.detail: Open CleanJibe on the iPhone and leave it in front of you for a minute. Bluetooth on, the watch next to it.

entries.term: CleanJibe is not offered in Apple's Watch app
entries.detail: Reinstall CleanJibe on the iPhone, then look again under *Available apps*.

entries.term: Garmin: CleanJibe is not in the activity list
entries.detail: Open Garmin Connect on the phone, let it sync, look again. The install can take a minute to reach the watch.
Check the activity is visible on intervals.icu first. The Garmin link can take a few minutes. Then sync again.

entries.term: Garmin: the ZIP will not open in CleanJibe
entries.detail: Unzip it on the computer and AirDrop the .fit file inside instead.
Garmin, the CleanJibe Apple Watch app, Apple's Workout app, any .fit, or Strava.
Apple: model and watchOS version, under Settings → General → About. Garmin: model and software version, under Settings → System → About.
Yes or no, and how long it took.
The session page. Was the track drawn? Were parts of it teal?
A permission you were never asked for. A "Nothing to import" screen. A NO GPS that never cleared. A crash. Wording you did not understand.
